text:
BP check, third of three.

Home readings averaging 148/92 over a fortnight. In clinic today 152/94 then 149/90.

Essential hypertension confirmed. Starting amlodipine 5 mg od.

He is worried because his father was on dialysis by 60 and his uncle had a stroke at 55.
Reassured that his own kidney function is normal.

Bloods last week: creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, eGFR above 90, ACR 0.8 mg/mmol, HbA1c 42 mmol/mol.

No proteinuria. No previous myocardial infarction and no known heart disease.

Review 4/52 with a BP diary. QRISK discussed, 9%, statin deferred for now.

Head injury. Fell off a ladder at home, about 2 m, landed on grass.

GCS 15 throughout. No loss of consciousness witnessed. Vomited once at the scene, not since.

No anticoagulant and no antiplatelet. Amlodipine only.

CT head within 8 hours per NICE: no acute intracranial injury, no skull fracture.

Impression is concussion with no intracranial injury.

His wife has epilepsy and asked whether the vomiting could mean he had had a seizure too.
Explained the difference.

Query post concussion syndrome if the headache persists beyond two weeks - GP to review.

Head injury advice given verbally and in writing. Wife will observe overnight.
